A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMI-based dataset distillation work. All 18 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.8, support reliable comparison. The appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, cross-architecture evaluations, ablations, and computational timing results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix A, including benchmark accuracies, ablations, and timing measurements.

M1.justification: The empirical CMI computation, combined distillation objective in Equation (11), sampling of pretrained networks, and class-wise computation in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same dataset distillation tasks on SVHN, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K, with the same cross-architecture scenarios. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the tables, including MIM4DD, SeqMatch, IID, DREAM, PDD, and the SDC comparison in Appendix A.1.

E3.justification: The IPC settings, Top-1 test accuracy metric, backbone and proxy architectures, training configurations, and cross-architecture evaluation procedures are unchanged, including the appendix experiments.

E4.justification: Both retain the same weighting-parameter sensitivity, pretraining/feature-space ablations, convergence analyses, teacher-architecture studies, and dataset visualizations in Section 5 and Appendix A.

E5.justification: Both specify five repetitions for standard and cross-architecture evaluations and retain the same mean and plus/minus reporting. No run-count or uncertainty-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 corrects IDC+CMI's improvement over IDC on SVHN at IPC=50 from 1.8 to 2.1 percentage points. The underlying accuracies remain 90.1±0.1 and 92.2±0.1, respectively. All other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions and derivations in Sections 3–4, Equations (1)–(11), and mathematical reasoning in the appendix are unchanged. The introduction clarifies descriptions of random variables without changing their formal construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about CMI regularization, reduced synthetic-data complexity, general applicability, and improved performance and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning class clustering, generalization, and efficiency remain unchanged. Appendix A.7 retains the same limitations concerning IPC=1, proxy-model selection, and the overhead of multiple pretrained teachers.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, implementation descriptions, class-wise pseudocode, RTX 3090 timing information, and the code-access URL are unchanged. The revised funding acknowledgement adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, Section 2 positioning, and Appendix A.1 comparisons with IID and SDC remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction replaces 'distillated information' with 'condensed information' and clarifies descriptions of the input, label, and output random variables. The funding acknowledgement is updated. Section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title is reflowed to avoid splitting 'Conditional' across lines, and Figure 4 is shifted slightly upward with a final period added to its caption. Figure content, table structures, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 fixes a verifiable arithmetic inconsistency in Table 1: 92.2 minus 90.1 is 2.1, not 1.8 percentage points. Clearer introductory variable descriptions also improve precision. These are limited reporting improvements; the method, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
